en: We had a look at the bubble sort algorithm,
a fairly simple and easy to implement
algorithm that tends to give us O,
so quadratic time complexity.
Maybe we can do better, and we can. Let's
now have a look at another sorting algorithm
which we can apply,
and that would be the quicksort algorithm.
Now, how does the Quicksort algorithm work?
It's also a fairly simple algorithm, I can
say that, and it will use recursion to sort
elements.
The idea on the Quicksort algorithm
is that you use pivot elements
to split the array into smaller chunks.
You simply choose one element in the array
and then you find out which elements in the
array are bigger, smaller, and equal than
the pivot element and you put those elements
into 3 different chunks, into 3 different
new arrays,
and then you repeat the process for those
arrays. So you pick a pivot element— often
that's simply the first element in the
array, so
you don't take the middle or anything like
that, but simply the first element because
the array is unsorted anyways—
and then you create 3 new arrays, a smaller
chunk or a smaller elements array
equal elements array and a larger elements
array.
And you then put the pivot element into that
center chunk, into that equal elements
chunk, and any other elements of the same
value would go into that same chunk. Smaller
elements go into that smaller chunk, into
that smaller elements array, and larger
elements go into the larger elements array.
So now we have 3 arrays with elements,
and now we simply
repeat that process. We create 3 new arrays,
and again, we choose a new pivot element.
And we do that in
every
array, by the way, not just in the large
elements array, but we would do this in
every array because we could have more items
than just 1 item in every array.
So we would repeat that process, pick a new
pivot element. And if we here on this slide
focus on the elements which were greater
than our old pivot element, we would split
this array into 3 new arrays in a recursive
step
and put our new pivot element into a new
equal elements array in that recursive
function, have a smaller chunk array and
have a larger chunk array. That's how it
would work. Now at the end of the algorithm,
we would therefore kind of end up with a
bunch of elements separated in separate
arrays and we would simply concatenate all
these arrays together and they would be
sorted correctly because of that splitting
we make in every recursive step.
Now that's the logic behind the Quicksort
algorithm. Now let's implement it in code.
